Subject: Question: Will Redwood train models on Centria prompts/responses?

Hi Ben —

We're kicking off our internal review for the new LLM integration and have a few specific privacy/regulatory questions we need answered before legal will sign the DPA addendum:

1) Do you ever use customer prompts/responses to further train or fine-tune Redwood models (or provide them to third-party training pipelines)?
2) If yes, can Centria get a contractually binding "no-train on customer content" commitment? If not, what opt-out mechanisms exist and how are they enforced?
3) How long are prompts and generated responses retained in logs, metrics, or debugging traces? Are there separate retention policies for embeddings/vector indexing?
4) We need SOC 2 evidence and a CAIQ snapshot that maps your controls for data isolation/retention. Also any SCC or DPA clause language you recommend for the no-train commitment.

We'd appreciate a concise one-page summary we can forward to legal plus links to the evidence you can provide.

Thanks — Evan
Evan Brooks
Director, Information Security
Centria Health

Hi Evan —

Thanks for the clear list — important questions. Looping in Monica (security & compliance lead on this account) and Laura (legal/contract owner) to pull evidence and draft contract language.

Quick answers up front, high-level:
- Redwood does not use customer content to train upstream public models by default.
- We offer a contractual "no-training" addendum for hosted customers that prevents any use of customer content for training unless explicit, signed opt-in is provided.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments: customer data never leaves their environment and is not used for Redwood model training.
- Retention: default interactive-debug logs are retained for 30 days; configurable retention tiers exist and shorter retention can be configured for enterprise customers. Embeddings/indexing can be configured to not persist beyond the session.

I'll send the one-page summary, SOC 2 excerpt, and a CAIQ snapshot in a follow-up. Monica — can you prepare the one-pager and attach the evidence we typically send to healthcare prospects? Laura — can you prepare suggested DPA addendum wording (no-train clause + audit evidence callouts)?

Best,
Ben

Subject: Re: Question: Will Redwood train models on Centria prompts/responses? (evidence + language)

Hi Evan —

Please find a concise summary below and the attachments referenced for SOC 2 and CAIQ snapshot. I'll quote the relevant technical controls and provide recommended contract wording after Ben/Laura review.

One-page summary (for legal):
- Default behavior: Customer prompts and generated outputs are not used to train Redwood public models.
- Contractual option: We offer a signed "No-Training Addendum" that legally prohibits Redwood from using any customer content (prompts, responses, embedding vectors, attachments) for any model training or improvement activities. This addendum is available for Hosted customers; Dedicated/Private deployments are excluded from training by architecture.
- Opt-out enforcement: Opt-out is implemented as an account-level flag (hosted) and enforced in our ingestion pipeline prior to any telemetry or transfer to training stores. Changes to the flag are recorded in audit logs and immutable events.
- Retention:
  - API request/response bodies (debug logs): default 30 days; can be reduced to 0/7/14/30/90 depending on contract.
  - Metrics/traces: aggregated metrics retained longer for platform health (configurable); no raw text is retained in aggregated metrics.
  - Embeddings/vector indexes: not persisted by default unless the customer explicitly creates an index or uses Redwood-managed vector store; customers may request immediate deletion of stored vectors.
- Evidence: Attached are a SOC 2 excerpt and CAIQ snapshot. Also attaching our internal "no-train playbook" which describes technical guardrails and audit controls.

Recommended DPA addendum snippet (suggested, non-binding):
"Redwood Inference shall not use Customer Content (including but not limited to prompts, completions, attachments, and embeddings) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning models used by Redwood unless Customer provides an explicit, documented, and signed opt-in. Redwood shall persist Customer Content only as set out in the DPA; Customer may request deletion of retained content at any time and Redwood shall comply within the timeframes set forth in the DPA. Redwood shall provide evidence of retention and deletion via audit logs or through an agreed process."

Attachments included: redwood-soc2-excerpt.pdf (PDF, 480KB stub), redwood-caiq-snapshot.pdf (PDF, 220KB stub), no-train-playbook.docx (DOCX, 65KB stub)

Let us know if you want a short call with our security engineering lead to walk through the ingestion/flag enforcement flow.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
